### Summary

Browser CDP connections could discard DNS pinning. In affected versions, OpenClaw validated one DNS result for a configured CDP hostname but raw WebSocket and Playwright transports performed a later independent resolution.

This advisory is scoped to configured remote CDP endpoints. It does not treat intentional local browser control as a vulnerability; the failed boundary was the SSRF policy that approved one destination but connected to another.

### Impact

An attacker who controlled an approved CDP hostname or its DNS answers could use rebinding to make the Gateway connect to a loopback, private, link-local, metadata, or other policy-denied address. Practical impact depended on remote CDP configuration, DNS timing, and services reachable from the Gateway host.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, disable hostname-based remote CDP endpoints or restrict them to trusted, stable infrastructure.
summary: Browser CDP connections could discard DNS pinning
